title: After the Apology
description:
A month since you apologized to your father.
He said 'It's fine.'
Today a call came from him.

choices.result_text:
He didn't say much — just asked how you were.
But the fact that he called — was the answer in itself.
The apology had melted something that had built up.

You talked briefly.
He talked about his health.
First call after an apology — awkward, but that was the beginning.

title: Your Father's Story
description:
Two months since you heard your father's story of his younger days.
For the first time then, he felt like a person — not just a father.
Today he brought up a similar story again.

choices.result_text:
He talked for an hour.
Inside that hour — was one man's whole life.
The time left to hear a parent's story — there isn't as much of it as you think.

You listened quietly.
His expression changed while he talked.
Listening — is sometimes everything.

title: After Going Home
description:
Two months since you rushed home for your father.
Since then, something in him shifted.
Today your mother called.
'He still talks about you coming that day.'

choices.result_text:
You put the next visit on the calendar.
The fact that he still remembered — was the answer that going was right.
Being busy and not going — those are different words.

choices.text: Tell your mother to look after him
choices.result_text:
'Make sure he's taking care of himself,' you said.
Mom said 'You should come by sometimes.'
There are things a phone call can't replace.

title: The Weight of Not Going
description:
Two months since you put off visiting your father because you were busy.
Today a text from him.
'Minjun. You doing okay.'

choices.result_text:
You called.
He said 'Been a while.'
A text was him thinking of his son.
Next time — you had to go in person.

You texted back 'I'm good.'
He replied 'Good, stay healthy.'
Two texts exchanged — that was where the relationship stood.

title: Sending Money Instead
description:
A month since you sent money instead of going in person.
Today a short text from your father.
'Got it. Thank you.'

choices.text: Say you'll come in person soon
choices.result_text:
'I'll come in person next time,' you said.
He said 'Don't worry if you're busy.'
'Don't worry if you're busy' — didn't mean don't come.

At least he said thank you.
But money couldn't stand in for being there.
You knew that.

title: After Saying You Were Fine
description:
Two months since you told your father 'I'm okay.'
You weren't, really.
Today he asked again.
'How are you these days. For real.'

choices.result_text:
'Honestly — it's been a bit rough,' you said.
Your father was quiet for a long moment, then: 'I see.'
Two words — that lifted two months of weight.

'Still fine,' you said.
He said '...Okay.'
The 'okay' felt like he already knew.
Parents know.

title: Being There for the Appointment
description:
Two months since you went into the consultation room with your father.
You heard what the doctor said directly.
Today the results of the next test came in.

choices.text: Check the results together with him
choices.result_text:
You heard 'Better this time' together.
Your father said quietly 'I see.'
Going into the room then — put you in the room for this moment too.

choices.text: Let him check on his own
choices.result_text:
He checked it himself.
Later he told you briefly: 'They said it's fine.'
Being there and being told — those are different things.

title: The Day It Was All Paid Off
description:
A month since you paid off the MLM debt completely.
Today the person you'd borrowed from reached out.
'Took long enough.'

choices.result_text:
'Thanks for waiting,' you said.
They replied: 'People who actually pay back are rarer than you'd think.'
Paying it back to the end — that was the measure of a person.

You kept it short: 'Done now.'
They kept it short too: 'Good for you.'
Some relationships don't need many words.

title: The Weight of Having Said No
description:
Three months since you turned down the MLM.
Today the acquaintance who pitched it sent a quiet message.
'I'm out. Lost everything.'

choices.result_text:
'Must be rough,' you said.
They replied: 'Glad you didn't get in. Sorry for trying.'
You were right to say no — and they weren't to blame.
Both were true.

You said 'That must've been hard.'
They went quiet for a moment.
You were glad you'd said no — but you didn't say that out loud.

title: After Holding the Line
description:
Two months since you held the line when you felt yourself being pulled in.
Today the urge came back.

choices.result_text:
You held it.
Hold it twice — and you can hold it a third time.
A line only becomes a line when you keep holding it.

Once became once.
'Just once' — that's always how it starts.
What you'd held before was now wasted.

title: Recovery in Progress
description:
You've been trying to stop.
Today marks two months.
It's not easy.

choices.result_text:
You wrote the date down.
Two months.
Seems small — but it was the product of a decision made every day.
The number became a reason.

choices.text: Feels like there's still so far to go
choices.result_text:
Still so far to go.
But you held yesterday and today.
'Still so far' doesn't mean giving up.
It means you're still going.

title: The Result of Putting It Off Twice
description:
You've put off the doctor twice.
Today your body got worse.
You couldn't put it off anymore.

choices.result_text:
You booked it.
The doctor said 'Why did it take this long?'
Delaying twice had made it worse.
No third time.

You held out.
A week later it got worse.
Some things aren't about toughness.
Your body says things louder when you ignore them.

title: The Friend's Recovery
description:
Three months since you heard your friend who'd been wiped out by MLM was recovering.
Today a call directly from them.
'I'm doing better these days.'

choices.result_text:
'Really glad,' you said.
They said 'Thanks for not judging and waiting.'
Not judging while waiting — had made this call possible.

choices.text: "That's amazing. How did you do it?"
choices.result_text:
They talked for a long time.
The story of holding on alone through the hardest of it.
Every person recovers differently.

title: What the Insurance Protected
description:
The jeonse deposit insurance you'd signed up for — when the landlord couldn't return the deposit, it came through.
The insurer stepped in and covered it.
You got the full deposit back.

choices.text: Sign up for insurance first on the next place too
choices.result_text:
You put insurance registration as the first item on the list.
A policy costing tens of thousands protected hundreds of millions.
Insurance wasn't a cost — it was the cover charge.

choices.text: What a relief. I got lucky.
choices.result_text:
Lucky.
But it wasn't luck — it was preparation.
When preparation feels like luck — that's the best kind of preparation.

title: Preparing to Move
description:
With the lease expiring, you've been looking for a new place.
Today you visited three real estate offices.
The gap between near-Gangnam and the outskirts felt stark.

choices.text: Go a little closer to Gangnam
choices.result_text:
It cost more.
But that neighborhood — would put the goal in sight every day.
Environment pulls your direction.

choices.text: Now is the time to save
choices.result_text:
You went further out.
You'd save more.
Where you live matters less than what you're doing — and that comes first.
